text_blocks.snippet: To help COVID-19 go away, focus on supportive care and, if eligible, specific treatments. Supportive care includes rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications for symptoms like fever and cough. For those at higher risk of severe illness, antiviral medications may be prescribed to prevent the virus from worsening, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on supportive care and, if eligible, specific treatments

list.snippet: Rest: Getting adequate rest allows your body's immune system to focus on fighting the virus.
Hydration: Drinking plenty of fluids, like water, helps to keep your body functioning properly and can help with symptom relief.
Symptom Management: Over-the-counter medications like fever reducers (e.g., acetaminophen or ibuprofen) and cough suppressants can help manage symptoms and improve comfort.
Certain antiviral medications can be prescribed for individuals at higher risk of severe COVID-19.
These medications work by targeting the virus and preventing it from replicating in the body.
According to the CDC, these treatments can help reduce the severity of the illness and prevent hospitalization.
To prevent the spread of the virus, it's important to isolate from others, especially if you are experiencing symptoms.
This includes staying home from work or school and avoiding close contact with people outside your household.
Individuals with weakened immune systems may need to isolate for longer periods.
If you have concerns about your symptoms or are at higher risk of complications, it's crucial to consult with a healthcare professional.
They can assess your individual situation and determine the most appropriate course of treatment.
